_meta.purpose: The single registry of every echolocation parameter the call dataset can store. Importers, validators and the page all read this file; none of them hardcode a parameter name. Adding a parameter is an edit to this file alone.
how_to_add_a_parameter: 1. Append an object to "parameters". Required keys: id, label, group, value_type, status, definition.
2. Numeric parameters also need: unit, sane_min, sane_max. Categorical ones need: values.

3. List every spelling you have seen in a source table under "aliases" (lowercased, punctuation-free). Importers match source columns through these, so an alias added here makes the next source import work without code changes.

4. If the literature disagrees about what the quantity means, say so in "ambiguity". That string is shown in the UI next to the value and is why a measurement can carry a quality_flag of 'definition_unstated'.
5. Set status to 'proposed' until at least one real source has been imported against it; 'core' is reserved for parameters the species card may display.
Never rename or delete an id that has been imported against. Deprecate instead: set status='deprecated' and add 'superseded_by'.

value_types.numeric: A measured quantity. Stored with statistic/unit/dispersion in the measurement record.
value_types.categorical: A coded property of the call. Stored with the same provenance as a number; 'values' is the closed vocabulary.
value_types.boolean: Present/absent claim. Recorded explicitly as false, never inferred from absence.

statistics.mean: Arithmetic mean, normally with an sd or se in the dispersion fields.
statistics.median: Median, normally with quartiles in value_min/value_max.
statistics.range: A span; use value_min and value_max, leave value empty.
statistics.single: One measurement from one call or one individual.
statistics.approximate: The source states a rounded or hedged central value ('around 6 ms', '~45 kHz') without naming a statistic. Kept distinct from mean so that hedged values are never silently treated as estimates of a population parameter.

quality_flags.unit_inferred: The source did not state a unit; it was inferred from context.
quality_flags.harmonic_ambiguous: Which harmonic the value describes is unclear.
quality_flags.definition_unstated: The source does not say how the quantity was measured (threshold, reference distance, rms vs peak), so it is not safely comparable across studies.
quality_flags.digitised_from_figure: Read off a plot rather than a printed value.
quality_flags.derived: Modelled or calculated by the source rather than measured.
quality_flags.suspect: Looks wrong; retained with the flag rather than dropped.

groups.signal_structure: What kind of signal it is — the categorical description of call design.
groups.temporal: Time-domain measurements of pulses and pulse trains.
groups.beam: Spatial properties of the emitted beam and its consequences.
groups.auditory: Properties of the receiver rather than the emitted call.
groups.covariate: Not call parameters, but routinely co-reported and needed to interpret them.

parameters.label: Signal type
parameters.definition: Overall time-frequency design of the pulse.

values.CF-FM: Long CF component followed by a terminal FM sweep.
values.FM-CF-FM: CF component preceded and followed by FM sweeps.
values.FM-QCF: Steep initial FM sweep flattening into a QCF tail.
values.none: No echolocation. A positive, sourced claim - not missing data.

parameters.label: Duty cycle class
parameters.definition: Whether the species belongs to the high-duty-cycle (Doppler-compensating CF) or low-duty-cycle guild.

values.low: Pulse occupies a small fraction of the cycle; emission and echo separated in time.
values.high: Pulse occupies a large fraction of the cycle; emission and echo overlap, separated in frequency.

parameters.label: Emission route
parameters.definition: Anatomical route through which the pulse leaves the bat.

values.nasal: Emitted through the nostrils, usually beam-shaped by a noseleaf.
values.tongue_click: Non-laryngeal click produced with the tongue.

parameters.label: Dominant harmonic
parameters.definition: Which harmonic carries most energy. 1 = fundamental. Rhinolophids and hipposiderids typically emphasise the second.
parameters.ambiguity: Sources differ on whether the fundamental is counted as harmonic 1 or harmonic 0. Records normalise to fundamental = 1.

parameters.label: Harmonics present
parameters.definition: Number of harmonics visible above the noise floor.
parameters.ambiguity: Depends entirely on recording SNR and microphone bandwidth; comparable only within a study.

parameters.label: Doppler shift compensation
parameters.definition: Whether the species lowers emitted frequency in flight to hold the echo at its acoustic fovea.

parameters.label: Peak frequency
parameters.definition: Frequency of maximum energy in the call's power spectrum.
parameters.ambiguity: Measured over the whole call in some studies and over the call body in others; FFT window and size change the value. Record the method's frequency_definition wherever stated.

parameters.label: Characteristic frequency
parameters.definition: Frequency at the point of lowest slope in the call body (Analook convention). Not interchangeable with peak frequency.
parameters.ambiguity: Anabat/Analook-derived; zero-crossing analysis yields values not directly comparable with full-spectrum measurements.

parameters.label: Start frequency
parameters.definition: Frequency at the onset of the pulse.
parameters.ambiguity: Threshold-dependent: where the sweep is judged to begin varies with the dB threshold used, which is often unstated. Sources that print 'highest frequency' or 'Fmax' usually mean this for a downward FM sweep, but those headings are registered to max_frequency because they are literal; map them by hand per source rather than by alias.

parameters.label: End frequency
parameters.definition: Frequency at the end of the pulse; the terminal frequency of an FM sweep.
parameters.ambiguity: Same threshold dependence as start_frequency. Many sources print 'minimum frequency' or 'Fmin' for this quantity, which is only equivalent when the sweep descends monotonically; those headings are registered to min_frequency, so a source using them for the sweep terminus must be mapped explicitly in its importer.

parameters.label: Minimum frequency
parameters.definition: Lowest frequency present in the pulse. Distinct from end_frequency for calls that do not sweep monotonically downward.

parameters.label: Maximum frequency
parameters.definition: Highest frequency present in the pulse.

parameters.label: Bandwidth
parameters.definition: Frequency range spanned by the pulse, max_frequency minus min_frequency.
parameters.ambiguity: Some sources report a power-relative bandwidth (-3 dB or -10 dB) under the same word; those belong in bandwidth_3db / bandwidth_10db.

parameters.label: -3 dB bandwidth
parameters.definition: Width of the spectrum at half power below the peak.

parameters.label: -10 dB bandwidth
parameters.definition: Width of the spectrum 10 dB below the peak.

parameters.label: CF component frequency
parameters.definition: Frequency of the constant-frequency component of a CF or CF-FM call.
parameters.ambiguity: In flight this is Doppler-compensated and therefore lower than the resting frequency; hand-held and free-flight values are not comparable. Check recording_condition before using.

parameters.label: Resting frequency
parameters.definition: CF frequency emitted by a stationary bat; the reference against which Doppler compensation is measured. The value that varies geographically in Rhinolophus clines.

parameters.label: Knee frequency
parameters.definition: Frequency at which the steep initial FM sweep flattens into the call body.

parameters.label: FM sweep rate
parameters.definition: Rate of frequency change through the modulated portion of the pulse.

parameters.label: Q factor
parameters.definition: Spectral sharpness, peak frequency divided by -3 dB bandwidth. High for CF specialists.
parameters.ambiguity: Some authors compute Q from -10 dB bandwidth instead, giving systematically lower values.

parameters.label: Pulse duration
parameters.definition: Length of a single pulse.
parameters.ambiguity: Threshold-dependent. Values measured from a spectrogram at an unstated dB threshold can differ by a factor of two from envelope-based measures.

parameters.label: CF component duration
parameters.definition: Length of the constant-frequency portion of a CF-FM pulse.

parameters.label: FM component duration
parameters.definition: Length of the frequency-modulated portion of a pulse.

parameters.label: Inter-pulse interval
parameters.definition: Time between consecutive pulses.
parameters.ambiguity: Measured start-to-start by some authors and end-to-start by others; the two differ by one pulse duration. Where the source states which, record it in the method; where it does not, flag the measurement 'definition_unstated'.

parameters.label: Pulse rate
parameters.definition: Pulses emitted per second. Rises sharply through the approach phase into the terminal buzz.

parameters.label: Duty cycle
parameters.definition: Percentage of time occupied by pulse emission.

parameters.label: Terminal buzz duration
parameters.definition: Length of the terminal buzz preceding a capture attempt.

parameters.label: Source level
parameters.definition: Emitted sound pressure level on the beam axis.
parameters.ambiguity: Meaningless without a reference distance (10 cm and 1 m are both in use - a 20 dB difference) and without stating whether the value is rms or peak-equivalent. Both belong in the method record; a source level lacking a stated reference distance must be flagged.

parameters.label: Beam half angle
parameters.definition: Angle from the beam axis at which intensity has fallen by a stated amount, usually -3 dB or -6 dB.
parameters.ambiguity: The dB criterion must be recorded; -3 dB and -6 dB half-angles are not comparable.

parameters.label: Directionality index
parameters.definition: On-axis intensity relative to the spatial average; higher values mean a narrower beam.

parameters.label: Detection distance
parameters.definition: Range at which the species is estimated to detect a target of stated size.
parameters.ambiguity: Almost always modelled rather than measured, and strongly dependent on the assumed target strength and atmospheric attenuation. Treat as derived unless the source demonstrates otherwise.

parameters.label: Moth detection distance
parameters.definition: Distance at which an eared moth detects the approaching bat. The inverse of detection_distance, which is the bat detecting a target - the two must never be merged.
parameters.ambiguity: Depends on the moth species, which auditory cell (A1 or A2) is used as the criterion, and the assumed hearing threshold. Record the criterion in notes; values using different criteria are not comparable.

parameters.label: Best hearing frequency
parameters.definition: Frequency of greatest auditory sensitivity from a behavioural or evoked-potential audiogram.

parameters.label: Acoustic fovea frequency
parameters.definition: Narrow frequency band of expanded cochlear representation in high-duty-cycle species; normally just above the resting frequency.

parameters.label: Body mass
parameters.definition: Body mass of the measured individuals. Correlates strongly with peak frequency and is needed for any allometric use of the dataset.

parameters.label: Forearm length
parameters.definition: Forearm length of the measured individuals; the standard size proxy in bat literature.

parameters.label: Wing aspect ratio
parameters.definition: Wingspan squared over wing area. Predicts foraging habitat and therefore expected call design.

parameters.label: Wing loading
parameters.definition: Body weight over wing area, in N/m2. Together with aspect ratio, places a species in the open/edge/clutter space.
